heckles.message: Replace Spy Hunt with Starwake
heckles.heckle:
You deleted a working Spy Hunt and pasted a whole new game over index.html in one commit, 587 lines added and 282 gone, like a bailout bill nobody read. The entire game now lives in one file with the CSS, the state machine and every story paragraph jammed into template strings, so good luck finding anything. You save progress with a try and an empty catch that swallows every error, so when localStorage dies the intern gets a silent shrug. Panel text goes through innerHTML in a dozen places and only some of it is wrapped in esc, a coin flip dressed as policy.

Fix it: Split the script and styles out of index.html into their own files. Fill the empty catch in save() and load() with at least a console warning. Run every innerHTML template through esc, not just the name fields. Drop the Google Fonts links or self host them. Archive Spy Hunt on a branch instead of nuking it.

heckles.message: accord2011v6 archive checkpoint 6999 pages
heckles.heckle:
Checkpoint 6999 pages. Not 7000, because apparently even the crawler is too lazy to round up. This commit rewrites ref/archive/accord2011v6 files like lighting-and-horns.jsonl and maintenance.jsonl with hundreds of added lines of scraped manual text, committed straight to main like a filibuster that never ends. A git repo is not a hard drive, intern. Every one of these checkpoints bloats history forever, and the repo you cloned for a car exploder is turning into a landfill of jsonl. The message tells nobody what changed, only a counter, so the log reads like a hostage note written by a script.

Fix it: Move ref/archive out of the repo into storage meant for big data, or at least into a separate repo. Add ref/archive to .gitignore and stop committing crawler output. Make the crawler commit once when it finishes instead of every 500 pages. Write messages that say what section was added.

heckles.message: accord2011 archive checkpoint 4207 pages
heckles.heckle:
Another checkpoint, this time for the plain accord2011 archive at 4207 pages, landing six minutes after the v6 one like two toddlers fighting over the same crayon. Two crawlers are hammering the same repo at the same time and both push to main, which is how you get merge conflicts, lost work and a history that looks like a government shutdown. New files such as specifications.jsonl and starting-and-charging.jsonl are added with no check that the text is even useful. The number in the message is the only thing you thought about.

Fix it: Run one crawler at a time or give each its own branch. Rebase before every push in the crawler script so the two stop racing each other. Validate each jsonl file before committing it. Stop committing partial section files that the next checkpoint rewrites anyway.

heckles.message: accord2011v6 archive checkpoint 6499 pages
heckles.heckle:
Checkpoint 6499, and the diff is another pile of jsonl lines appended to the same v6 files, with each line holding a whole manual page as one giant string. A single line of that Heating and Air Conditioning Technical Service Bulletins record runs on for miles, so git cannot diff it and you cannot review it. Every checkpoint re-adds duplicated headers inside the text, like Customer Interest repeated back to back. It is like a campaign promise: lots of volume, nothing you can verify. The repo is a car exploder app and you are using it as a scraping dump.

Fix it: Strip the repeated headings in the crawler before writing to ref/archive. Store one record per file or compress the archive instead of megabyte lines. Dedupe records by path so rewrites stop growing. Keep the crawl data out of the app repo entirely.

heckles.message: accord2011 archive checkpoint 3707 pages
heckles.heckle:
Checkpoint 3707 for accord2011, the exact same commit as the last one with a smaller number, because the intern found a single idea and is riding it into the ground. Five hundred pages per push, on a timer, to main, with no human reading anything. The diff is just more jsonl in ref/archive/accord2011, and nothing in it touches the exploder, the three.js scene or the UI the repo exists for. That is not development, that is a cron job with a commit button.

Fix it: Commit crawl output on a schedule of days, not minutes. Put the crawler in tools with a README so someone knows it exists. Add a size check so the repo cannot grow past a sane limit. Rename the commits to name the section added.

heckles.message: accord2011v6 archive checkpoint 5999 pages
heckles.heckle:
Checkpoint 5999 pages. Ladies and gentlemen, one page short of a round number, which is also how I would describe the person running this crawler. It is the sixth hour of the same message with a bigger counter, and the v6 jsonl files in ref/archive/accord2011v6 keep growing while the app code sits untouched. Nobody is reviewing this, nobody can review this, and git history is now a ledger of a script talking to itself. Hand this to a grown up.

Fix it: Gitignore ref/archive and publish the data as a release or storage file. Squash these checkpoints before they bury the real history. Make the crawler resume from a local file, not from git commits. Put a page limit in tools so it stops on its own.

heckles.message: accord2011 archive checkpoint 3207 pages
heckles.heckle:
Checkpoint 3207. Five hundred more pages, five hundred more reasons to take the keyboard away. The diff drops another batch of manual sections into ref/archive/accord2011 and the repo gets fatter and the commit message gets dumber. Anyone cloning this to look at the exploder now downloads a whole service manual they did not ask for, which is the software version of a bill with forty riders attached. This is a repeat offense, and the repeat is the problem.

Fix it: Keep the archive in a separate data repo and fetch it only when needed. Use git LFS or release assets if the files must live near the code. Add the crawl folder to .gitignore today. Stop pushing from the crawler loop.

heckles.message: accord2011v6 archive checkpoint 5499 pages
heckles.heckle:
Checkpoint 5499. Two crawlers, two alternating commit streams, one repo, and zero adult supervision. The v6 and plain accord archives take turns pushing, so history reads like a tennis match nobody is watching. Each push is mostly appended lines to existing jsonl files in ref/archive/accord2011v6, so you are storing the same growing file over and over as new blobs. The commit message is a number. The number is not information. I have seen better changelogs on a ransom note.

Fix it: Merge the two crawlers into one job with one commit at the end. Write the archive to a single compressed file instead of dozens of rewritten jsonl files. Remove ref/archive from tracking. Use real messages.

heckles.message: accord2011 archive checkpoint 2707 pages
heckles.heckle:
Checkpoint 2707, a clean 500 changed lines across just three files, which means each file is being rewritten with giant single line records again. You could push this crawler a thousand times and the only thing you would learn is how long GitHub tolerates abuse. There is no sign anyone ever opened one of these jsonl files to see if the scraped text is usable, since the earlier catalog crawl in this same repo came back as an empty array of 404s. Wow. Scale before proof, just like a federal budget.

Fix it: Open a sample jsonl record and verify the text is clean before crawling thousands of pages. Fix tools/fetch_catalog.py so ref/parts stops being empty. Stop committing the archive. Add a test that fails if a record has no real text.

heckles.message: accord2011v6 archive checkpoint 4999 pages
heckles.heckle:
Checkpoint 4999 pages, ten files changed, 236 lines, and still no sign of the exploder getting better. Files like engine-cooling-and-exhaust.jsonl and instrument-panel-gauges-and-warning-indicators.jsonl are regrown over and over, which is how you turn a small hobby repo into a disk space crisis. The only information in the commit is a counter, and the counter is also wrong by one every time, 4999 instead of 5000, like the crawler flinches at the finish line. This is exactly the sort of thing you hand a trainee and then regret.

Fix it: Move the archive out of main and into storage that expects big files. Make the crawler round to clean batch sizes and say what it fetched. Squash the checkpoint pile into one commit. Get back to the actual exploder.

heckles.message: Cap the machine card size when zoomed in
heckles.heckle:
Your cap on the card scale in index.html is a Math.min with four arguments in one line, and two of them divide by card.offsetWidth and card.offsetHeight. If the card is hidden or not laid out yet, that is a divide by zero and k becomes Infinity or NaN, and then the whole card goes sideways like a budget negotiation. The changelog entry is also dated the same day as the entry right under it, so you are stacking tiny tweaks on a feature that shipped hours ago. Cramped phones are exactly where a thirty percent height cap makes the card unreadable.

Fix it: Guard card.offsetWidth and card.offsetHeight against zero before dividing in the zoom scale line of index.html. Test the cap on a small phone screen so the text stays legible. Fold same day changelog entries in CHANGELOG.md into one.

heckles.message: Fill canvas with any preset until the screen is covered
heckles.heckle:
Look at that one line in index.html: FILLS and FILL_NAMES now carry a fourth mode called rules, labeled Current rules, and the whole file is one giant minified wall where PRESET_NAMES is a single line the length of a tax code. You added a fill style by hand editing a line that long, and I would bet the intern has not scrolled sideways far enough to see the end. The commit message promises covering the screen with any preset, but the diff is 28 added lines in one html file with no test and no word on what stops the loop when the screen never fills. That is a campaign promise with a spinner.

Fix it: Add a hard cap on the fill loop in index.html so it cannot run forever. Break the PRESET_NAMES line into one entry per line. Rename the rules fill so the label says what it does.

heckles.message: Catalog crawler: tighter part name match
heckles.heckle:
A tighter regex, committed forty seconds after the crawler it fixes, and seconds before the run that found nothing. part_re in tools/fetch_catalog.py is now a negative lookahead sandwich nobody can read, and you tuned it blind against pages that 404 anyway. heckles.message: Dealer catalog part number crawler
heckles.heckle:

heckles.message: BUY sheet: Safelite for glass, Discount Tire for tires and wheels; tire sizes
heckles.heckle:

heckles.message: Info card pops up above the tapped machine and scales with zoom
heckles.heckle:
You moved the info card from a sane bottom sheet into a floating bubble pinned over the machine, scaled by zoom. In #card you set width to min(300px,78vw) and pointer-events none, then patched buttons back on with #card button, which is duct tape on a decision. On a phone, a card that shrinks as you zoom out gets unreadably tiny, and the max-height and overflow rules got deleted, so a long card can run off screen. The changelog brags it stays on screen. Nothing in the diff proves it.

Fix it: Restore a max-height and overflow auto on #card in index.html. Set a minimum scale so the card never drops below readable text. Test it on a narrow phone width with a machine at the screen edge.

heckles.message: Prius part numbers on the card and print sheet, BUY sheet, add Prius spark plugs
heckles.heckle:
One commit that does part numbers, print sheet, buy sheet, search links and new spark plug meshes. That is five commits wearing a trench coat. The new ref/parts/prius.json is committed here as a 14 line file, and the very next commits expand it to over a hundred lines, so churn is the whole plan. index.html now has another esc function and cardHTML builds a whole page by string concatenation on one monster line, which is an injection bug waiting for a part name with a quote in it.

heckles.message: Diagram viewer sits above the menu button
heckles.heckle:
The fix for a layering bug is bumping z-index from 20 to 40 in viewDiagram in index.html. That is the stacking context version of turning the volume up on a broken speaker. You have a pile of magic z-index numbers scattered through inline cssText strings and you are now just guessing bigger ones. The next overlay you add will need 41 and the one after that 99999, like a bailout that keeps needing more money.

Fix it: Collect all z-index values into CSS variables in index.html. Move the cssText strings in viewDiagram into a class. Document which overlay goes on top of which.

heckles.message: Print sheet fits on one page, drops on-screen hints
heckles.heckle:
A one line commit that edits a single enormous string in cardHTML inside index.html. The patch is a wall of inline CSS jammed into one line, so reviewing it means scrolling sideways like it is 1998. Fits on one page means you eyeballed it with one part and called it done, because a long part name and a tall diagram will happily spill to page two. The intern who writes print CSS inside a JS string literal should not be allowed near stylesheets.

Fix it: Move the print styles in cardHTML into a style block with an @media print and @page rule. Test with the longest part name and the tallest diagram. Break the string across lines so a diff can be read.

heckles.message: Card taps no longer hit the parts behind it; Print button and tap to enlarge diagram
heckles.heckle:
This one adds a new esc helper, cardHTML, CARD_HIT and a Print button to index.html in one burst, and the first line of the fix is a global object CARD_HIT with null fields that exist to be mutated from anywhere. Taps hitting the parts behind the card was a bug you created yourself two commits of features ago. The fix commit also bolts on new features, so nobody can tell what fixed what. Subtle as a filibuster, and about as productive.

Fix it: Separate the tap bug fix from the Print and enlarge features. Replace the CARD_HIT global with a small closure or a plain handler in index.html. Check that esc is not already defined elsewhere in the file.

heckles.message: Mirror both cars so the steering wheel is on the left
heckles.heckle:
Your car models were built backwards and the fix is ROOT.scale.z=-1 on a group, flipping the whole world like a politician flipping on a vote. A negative scale inverts triangle winding, so lighting, backface culling and normals on every mesh in index.html can turn inside out, and you also have a comment saying z points to the left while another says right. Now the blueprint overlay in bp() needed edits too, because the mirror leaks into everything.

Fix it: Fix the mesh coordinates in index.html instead of mirroring ROOT. If the mirror stays, set material side to DoubleSide or flip the winding on mirrored geometry. Reconcile the two contradictory z-axis comments.

140 calls in a single file: 63 lines, 47 removes, 22 symbols and 8 hatches, so the bot builds a thing and tears down half of it in the same breath, like a congress that passes a bill and repeals it before lunch. The ids 38433 and 38434 get removed at the top of the file, meaning this agent is cleaning up its own last mess one turn late. One sign symbol carries a long paragraph of fiction about a town clock in its meta text, a giant string baked into a data file.

heckles.message: Prius: clean panel seams, smooth wheel arches, finer loft; Accord: air cleaner and valve cover under hood
heckles.heckle:

heckles.message: Manual crawler: fetch with curl, log failures
heckles.heckle:

heckles.message: Restore labels and info card in the render loop; label assemblies when the car is exploded
heckles.heckle:

Another steward turn, another one line minified JSON blob in contrib/steward/2026-11-20T191539.json that no human could review if they tried. It is thousands of characters of place_symbol and place_line calls with hardcoded six digit coordinates, wood poles, conductors, and telephone cable sagging by hand typed z values. Merging it through a pull request is a bit of theater, since nobody reads it, and the review is a rubber stamp like a committee hearing nobody attends. If a pole is misplaced by a few meters, you will never find it in a single unbroken line.

Fix it: Pretty print the contrib JSON or one call per line so diffs are reviewable. Add a validation check that rejects out of range coordinates before the merge. Stop approving these by reflex. Have the steward write a short summary file next to each turn.

heckles.message: Trigger production build
heckles.heckle:
An empty commit. Zero files changed, and the intern still found a way to waste my morning. Trigger production build is not a message, it is a cry for help from someone who does not know how a Vercel deploy works. The previous commit landed and the deploy did not fire, so instead of finding out why, you pushed nothing and prayed. That is a bailout with no accountability: money spent, nothing fixed, no explanation given. Do not let me see another one of these.

Fix it: Check the Vercel project's git link for this repo instead of pushing empty commits. If a redeploy is truly needed, use the dashboard redeploy button or the CLI. Squash this noise out of the history next time. Put the real reason for the missed build in the commit message.

heckles.message: Lane Listener drive-thru order listener
heckles.heckle:
Five hundred fifteen lines of index.html dumped in one commit, and the intern called it a drive-thru listener like it was a product launch. Every rule lives inline: the tokenize and parse functions, the price math, the learned aliases in localStorage, and the whole stylesheet crammed into one file with no tests. The render code is a swamp of innerHTML string concatenation, so one missed esc call turns a customer's spoken order into script injection. The speech setup grabs webkitSpeechRecognition and just hopes the browser has it, with no visible fallback story. This is a filibuster in file form: loud, long, and nothing gets decided.

Fix it: Split the script out of index.html into its own file so it can be tested. Replace the innerHTML concatenation in the render functions with textContent or createElement. Add a visible fallback when SpeechRecognition is missing. Give the one letter classes real names. Write a test for tokenize and parse before this ships.

heckles.message: Raise the Raineurysm Puzzle score ceiling for twenty four levels
heckles.heckle:
You bumped the score max for raineurysm-puzzle in api/_games.js from 60000 to 150000 by guessing, because there is no math or comment anywhere that says why 150000 and not 149000 or a million. The ceiling is the only thing standing between this hub and a cheater posting a fake high score, and you moved it like a senator adding a rider at midnight. Then the changelog got a new v2026.11.19r entry stacked above entries dated the 17th and the 18th, so your dates go 19, 17, 18 like a calendar run by a filibuster. The README Latest change line now credits the wrong entry too.

Fix it: Write down how 150000 was derived, ideally from the level count times a per level maximum. Keep perSecond at 300 in line with the new ceiling or justify why it stays. Sort CHANGELOG.md so the newest entry is really first. Check that the README Latest change line matches the real newest entry.

heckles.message: Isometric lock shape mode
heckles.heckle:
Isometric lock mode, and the first thing you did was declare var isoLock=false in the middle of the file between helper functions like a campaign promise tossed into a budget bill. isoAxes returns two hardcoded arrays of radians typed by hand, and isoNext is a loop that matches angles with a 1e-6 epsilon, which is a fancy way of praying. The aim branch in the steering code grew an if else ladder with magic numbers, 0.2 and 0.15 and 0.5, that nobody including you can explain. Also isoNext sits there unused as far as this diff shows. Dead code on day one, impressive for something that cannot even spell its own toggle.

Fix it: Delete isoNext if nothing calls it. Name the magic numbers 0.2, 0.15 and 0.5 as constants. Move isoLock up with the other state variables. Check that isoSnap behaves when iso is off. Add a comment explaining why the axes differ per mode.

heckles.message: Memory mode: replay rounds that learn from collisions
heckles.heckle:
A memory mode dropped into the same single index.html, because splitting files is apparently a government program you refuse to fund. You added a Memory button, then smeared a pile of globals across the file: memOn, memRun, memStart, memSeed, memRng, memRound, memT, scars, memRngs, memCur, memFix. That is eleven loose variables, a bailout package for a state you never planned. Worse, newPipe now mutates memCur inside the constructor, and commit quietly stops calling snapshot whenever memOn is true, so undo goes dark without a word. The intern built a feature that learns from collisions and cannot learn from its own naming.

Fix it: Wrap the memory globals in one object so they stop polluting the file. Move the memCur side effect out of newPipe. Make the undo behavior in commit explicit when memOn is true. Add a way to switch Memory off cleanly. Give hashStr a comment or a test.

heckles.message: Cloth weave: over only single lines, under and stay under for bundles
heckles.heckle:
Four presets, basket, crochet, lace and doily, got their weave flipped from alternate to a brand new cloth string, and the commit message reads like a ransom note written by someone who lost the dictionary. The whole change lives in one giant index.html where the preset table is a wall of comma soup that no human could diff without a stiff drink. You added cloth to WEAVE_NAMES, which is the only thing you bothered to wire visibly, so I am betting the actual over and under logic is hiding somewhere you forgot to touch. Nineteen lines, and a handful of them are the same string typed four times. Truly the filibuster of find and replace.

Fix it: Pull the weave strings in the preset table into one constant instead of retyping cloth four times. Explain in the commit message what cloth actually does. Test that cloth falls back safely anywhere the code still only knows alternate. Split index.html before it eats the repo.

heckles.message: Skin locked per map, heart and strip landmarks, city towers scale with district size
heckles.heckle:
A hundred and forty six lines added to one index.html, because apparently the intern thinks a file is a landfill. You deleted the Skin button from the top bar and then bolted a new #scount button rule on, so the layout shuffles like a cabinet after a filibuster. Skins locked per map means the player loses a choice, and the commit message promises heart and strip landmarks like a campaign pledge with no budget. City towers scaling with district size is more math buried in the same giant script with no tests.

Fix it: Split the skin CSS and the map logic out of index.html into separate files. Check that the #scount button rule does not squeeze the top bar on a narrow phone. Tell the player why the skin is locked instead of silently removing the Skin button. Write one test for tower scaling.

heckles.message: West and Bunker skins, Meadow fields with scoring and Biggest Meadow record
heckles.heckle:
Three hundred and thirty five lines in one commit. West skin, Bunker skin, Meadow scoring, and a record, all dumped in index.html like a bailout bill with forty riders nobody read. The body.ww block is a wall of one line CSS with hardcoded browns and a Georgia font stack, copied from the War skin with the colors swapped, which is what an intern does when the deadline is in five minutes. The Meadow scoring and the record sit in the same inline script as everything else, so one typo takes the whole game down.

Fix it: Move the skin palettes into CSS variables instead of cloning whole body.ww and body.w blocks. Pull Meadow scoring out of the giant inline script. Guard the Biggest Meadow record against bad localStorage data. Ship one feature per commit.

heckles.message: War skin: army map with trenches, bases, HQs and marching soldiers
heckles.heckle:
A War skin with trenches, bases, HQs and marching soldiers, all in the same index.html that is already groaning. The new body.w block is a pile of hardcoded olive and khaki hex colors with a Courier New font, copy pasted from the other skins with the paint changed. Marching soldiers means a new animation loop, and I see no sign anyone checked what it does to a phone battery. Your skin system is now a heap of body letters like w, c and ww, which reads like a ransom note.

Fix it: Give the skin classes real names instead of w, c and ww in index.html. Share one skin template and override only the colors. Cap the soldier animation frame rate and pause it when the tab is hidden. Stop growing a single file past the point of sanity.

Another steward pull request, another one line minified JSON blob in contrib/steward, merged with a button click like a rubber stamp. The payload is a place_hatch call for a crosswalk on a street, with six digit coordinates and a hatch spacing of 610. Nobody can review a single minified line, and the merge is the only quality gate, which is government efficiency at its finest. The bot cannot even keep its timestamp name consistent without human cleanup.

Fix it: Pretty print the contrib/steward JSON so a diff means something. Add a schema check that rejects a bad place_hatch call before merge. Stop merging these by hand and let a workflow validate and merge them.

heckles.message: Add Teardown tab, merge Pipeline Builder in as Builder tab
heckles.heckle:
Seven hundred and forty nine lines into index.html for a Teardown tab with sixty one hand typed products, and a Pipeline Builder smashed in as a tab, like merging two failing departments and calling it reform. The second style block is a late patch tacked on after the first one, with fresh pb and td classes beside the comic skin rules. The changelog line is one giant paragraph that nobody will read. Every layer is marked known or inferred, which is a polite way of admitting you are guessing.

Fix it: Move the sixty one product records out of index.html into a data file. Fold the second style block into the main stylesheet. Cut the CHANGELOG.md entry down to two sentences. Check the new tabs on a small phone.

The grok bot pushed straight to the branch again with no pull request, no review and no gate, like a senator voting on a bill he never read. The file contrib/grok/2026-11-19T172357.json is one minified line of place_line calls with negative coordinates for a Mesquite House wall, plus door checks stuffed into meta arrays. Nothing proves the walls close or the door checks pass. A direct push under the developer login means the history cannot tell the bot from the intern.

Fix it: Make the grok bot open a pull request like the other bots. Validate the door height and door width checks in the JSON before it lands. Format the file so a human can read it. Give the bot its own commit author.

heckles.message: Per pipe and shifting line colors
heckles.heckle:
Per pipe and shifting colors, in a single index.html, with a new inkMode global and a pipeInk function that returns a raw hsl string rebuilt on every call. The strokeEdgeShift function breaks an edge into six point chunks inside a loop, so the draw path does string building per segment like it is paying by the allocation. Three modes named all, pipe and shift live in loose var globals with matching display names in another object, so adding a fourth means editing three places. Nice little rainbow, intern, shame about the plumbing.

Fix it: Cache the hsl strings in pipeInk in index.html instead of rebuilding them per segment. Put the ink modes in one table. Check that p.ink and p.hue exist for old saved pipes. Test shifting mode on a long pipe for frame drops.

heckles.message: Full screen button
heckles.heckle:
A Full screen button, wired by hand with a fixed position hack, in a file that already has too many buttons. The new #fsBtn sits absolute at the bottom right with a z-index of 5 and fades to 0.55 opacity in full screen, so it hovers over the canvas right where a thumb will draw. The body.fs rule hides the bar and status pill, so once you are in there the only way out is the ghost button. There is no sign of a real fullscreen API fallback for phones that refuse it.

Fix it: Check that requestFullscreen actually exists in index.html and fall back gracefully on iPhones. Move #fsBtn away from the drawing area. Give the player an obvious exit that is not a faded button.

heckles.message: High scores: post each shift to the Score Hub, per task boards in the review and the menu
heckles.heckle:
Fifty five lines added to just-five-more-v1.html so the game can post scores to a public hub, and I see the board styles stacked right on top of the math styles like laundry on a chair. A three letter name input with text-transform uppercase is the only identity check, so anyone can post anything. The fixed height 150px board will clip on a small phone, and the grid of two buttons with 12px text is cramped. Posting every shift to a hub with no proof the score is real is a rigged election with extra steps.

Fix it: Validate the score on the server in the hub instead of trusting the client in just-five-more-v1.html. Let the board height flex on small screens. Handle a failed post with a visible retry. Debounce the post button so one shift cannot spam the hub.

heckles.message: Connector tiles for every edge combination and auto hole filling
heckles.heckle:
An IIFE that brute forces every four edge combination out of the letters C, R, F and W with four nested loops, then pushes filler tiles into DEFS at load time. It is clever in the way a lit match in a barn is clever. The weights are a magic .12 and the lake flag is a one line ternary nobody can read. Every page load now burns cycles building tiles that could be a static list. The nested loops use a, b, c and e as variable names, because apparently d was taken and imagination was not.

Fix it: Name the loop variables and the .12 weight in index.html. Build the connector list once and check it in instead of generating it on load. Add a test that no edge pattern is missing. Explain the lake rule in a comment.

heckles.message: Highways, roundabouts, intersections, fabric weaves, stair presets and skin, picture stamps, radiant pop and under the sea themes, fish, fill canvas
heckles.heckle:
One commit, 171 lines added to a single index.html, and it ships fourteen picture stamps, eleven new pattern styles, two fill buttons and a new rules hint paragraph like a bailout bill with every rider the committee could staple on. The stampSel dropdown hardcodes fourteen options in markup while the drawing for each lives somewhere else, so adding a fifteenth means editing two places, which is how an intern builds a filibuster. The pattern select is now a wall of twenty something options on a phone screen. The commit message is a grocery list, because you could not decide what the commit was about, and neither could I. Did you learn version control from the back of a cereal box?

Fix it: Split this into one commit per feature so the history is readable. Build the stamp options from a single stamps object in index.html instead of hand typing the select. Group the pattern select with optgroups so mobile users can find anything. Move the rules hint text out of the markup into data.

heckles.message: City skin redrawn as detailed illustrations with cached tile art and lit 3D buildings
heckles.heckle:
You redrew the whole City skin and managed to touch 220 lines of a single index.html, rewriting every body.c selector like a campaign promise nobody asked for. Swapping blue and yellow for beige and teal is a paint job on a file that still holds every skin as hand pasted CSS blocks, so the next skin means another stack of body.x lines. The message claims cached tile art and lit 3D buildings, yet the diff is mostly color values, so either the message lies or the real work is buried where nobody can review it. Hex codes repeated forty times with no variables is how you get a government shutdown in stylesheet form. I have seen interns with more discipline and less caffeine.

Fix it: Define the skin colors as CSS custom properties in index.html and reference them from the body.c rules. Split the cache and building drawing into its own commit. Move SKINS and the skin CSS out of the single file. Write a commit message that matches the diff.

heckles.message: City skin with 3D towers in iso, full River tile set, skin-aware names
heckles.heckle:
Two hundred lines landing in a single index.html, and the new City skin is a pile of body.c selectors bolted onto a file that already had body.g, body.k and whatever else you stapled on last week. Skins as copy pasted CSS blocks is a zoning board approving every shack that shows up with a form. Light grey and blue also means the dark themes that rescued your eyes are now optional, which is how you get a game that looks like a tax portal. Iso towers drawn inline in the same file means one typo and the whole map goes down, and you ship with no tests like a campaign promise ships with no plan.

Fix it: Move each skin into a data object instead of a new body class in index.html. Split the drawing code out of the page into its own script file. Check the City skin on a phone width, because the bottom bar is cramped. Add one smoke test that loads every skin.

heckles.message: Circuit style with AC and DC boards, schematic parts and legend; Cyber, Color Pop and Escher Remix skins with new tile patterns
heckles.heckle:
Four new skins and a circuit style in one commit, all dumped into the same index.html like a spending bill with nine riders nobody read. The .cp-body, .cp-line and .cp-hot classes are hardcoded hex colors, #24382c and #ff7a00 sprayed everywhere instead of the CSS variables you already defined, so the skins you just added cannot even be themed. The .ps-power .valve-arrow selector got patched with a comma instead of a real rule, which is duct tape on a bailout. Pretty sure the intern thinks a commit is a place to hide things.

Fix it: Replace the hardcoded hex values in the .cp-* rules in index.html with the existing CSS variables. Split the circuit, cyber and Escher skins into separate commits next time. Pull the SVG part builders out of the one giant file. Test the legend on a narrow phone screen.

heckles.message: Synth sounds with mute button, one way check valves, vault difficulty levels; shuffled vault chips; no stale clear cards after leaving Pipes
heckles.heckle:
This commit is five features and a bug fix wearing a trench coat. Synth sounds, a mute button, check valves, vault difficulty and a stale card fix all landed together in index.html, so if any one breaks you get to bisect a sandwich. The new .sound-btn has a 36 pixel hit area jammed next to the hamburger in .top-left with a 4 pixel gap, which on a phone is a fat finger lottery. Audio that starts with no mute memory is also how you get yelled at on a bus. The stale clear card fix tells me you knew the state handling was shaky and shipped anyway.

Fix it: Store the mute choice in localStorage so it survives a reload. Widen the gap between .menu-btn and .sound-btn in index.html. One feature per commit from here on. Add a guard that resets card state whenever the mode changes, not only when leaving Pipes.

heckles.message: Tile Spinner Vault accepts difficulty-scaled scores up to 3000
heckles.heckle:
You raised the vault max from 1000 to 3000 and doubled perSecond to 200 in api/_games.js, which is a cheat code with a changelog. Anyone who can hit the score endpoint can now post a 3000 in two seconds and sit atop the board like a lobbyist at a committee hearing. The perSecond limit is the only thing guarding the leaderboard, and you loosened it because your own client got rejected. That is fixing the referee instead of the game. Also this is the third changelog line for a single afternoon, in a file full of v2026.11.18b and c, which reads like a filibuster in version numbers.

Fix it: Validate the difficulty multiplier on the server in api/_games.js instead of just raising max. Tie perSecond to the difficulty so Easy cannot post an Expert score. Merge the same day changelog entries in CHANGELOG.md into one.

heckles.message: Pipe styles (classic, water mains, streets, power lines) and Big boards in three sizes; hide vault panel outside Play
heckles.heckle:
Pipe styles and three Big board sizes in one shot, and the CSS grew pole, house, house-lit and pseg classes with colors sprinkled in as raw hex like #7a5a3a and #ffd23a. The .ps-streets, .ps-power and .ps-water pipe-base overrides are three copies of the same rule with different paint, the kind of cloning that gets a department defunded. The statA line now checks P.big in a ternary inside the render function, so every mode keeps getting one more special case welded onto the same if chain. That chain is a tax code at this point.

Fix it: Collapse the three .ps-* pipe-base rules in index.html into one rule driven by CSS variables. Replace the mode if chain in the stats render with a lookup table. Keep the new hex colors in one palette block. Check the Big boards on a small phone.

heckles.message: Vault: blank ring on every junction, five hide digits, the rest are decoys
heckles.heckle:
A blank ring on every junction and most of them decoys. Congratulations, you built a game where the main mechanic is clicking on nothing. The hint text now literally says most rings are empty decoys, which is you admitting the design needs an apology on screen. The vault-ring rule gained a transition on fill, stroke and opacity all at once, on every ring on a big board, which is a nice way to make a cheap phone cry. And the dashed .vault-spot.empty rings at 0.45 opacity will be nearly invisible outside, so players will be tapping fog.

Fix it: Drop the transition on stroke and opacity in .vault-ring in index.html for large boards. Raise the contrast of .vault-spot.empty so decoys are readable in sunlight. Rewrite the hint text so it explains the goal instead of confessing the design.

heckles.message: Post Rush, Pipes and Vault scores to the score hub; tap outside a card to close it
heckles.heckle:
You wired score posting into the game card with a three letter tag input, which means the entire leaderboard identity system is a text box and a prayer. No auth, no rate limit on the client, and a shared hub that now trusts whatever the page sends it. The .post-tag field is 76 pixels wide with letter spacing of 0.2em, which on a phone will clip a three letter tag like a cheap suit. Tap outside a card to close it also means a stray thumb during a score entry throws the whole run away. Nice touch for the intern who loves lost data.

Fix it: Do not close the card in the index.html tap handler while the .post-tag input has focus or text. Add a client side cooldown on the score post. Widen .post-tag so the letters are not clipped. Make the server in the score hub reject empty tags.

heckles.message: Register Tile Spinner rush, pipes and vault boards
heckles.heckle:
Three new boards stuffed into api/_games.js, and look at the numbers you made up. Rush max 500 at one per second, vault max 1000 at 100 per second, pipes max 100000 over 400 days. Those limits are guesses with decimal places missing, like a budget projection written on a napkin. The vault one was wrong within the hour, since the very next commit had to raise it, so you shipped a config you never tested against your own game. The changelog entry labelled v2026.11.18b also skips a plain v2026.11.18 on the same day, a version scheme invented while falling down stairs.

Fix it: Play each board once and set max and perSecond from real runs in api/_games.js. Write the vault limit with its difficulty multiplier from the start. Fix the version label in CHANGELOG.md so it is not a b with no a.

heckles.message: Vault digits sit on the real yellow match dots; pips track real match progress; near-match hint glow
heckles.heckle:
So the vault digits were NOT sitting on the real match dots until now. That means the previous vault commit shipped a puzzle whose answers were in the wrong place, and you are patching a bug the same afternoon like an agency issuing a correction to its own press release. The new vertexProgress function has a hex branch, a square branch and a pile of special cases in the same index.html, and it calls tileMap.get with a template string key for every vertex on every render, which is a garbage collector protest waiting to happen. Fifty one lines deleted and ninety added to move dots, and not one test.

Fix it: Cache the tileMap key strings in vertexProgress in index.html instead of rebuilding them every render. Put the hex and square branches into separate small functions. Add a test that the vault digits land on lit match vertices for every grid type.

heckles.message: Completion chimes, record celebration, player outlines, bot opponents
heckles.heckle:
Bot opponents, chimes, outlines and a record celebration in one commit to index.html, and the bot logic landed in a file that also holds the rules text as raw HTML. You even jammed two paragraphs on one line with a stray closing p tag like a rider on a defense bill. The how to play text now says bots take their turns on their own, with zero word on how smart they are, because the answer is probably a random number generator wearing a tie. A chime per tile rising in pitch means a ten tile castle sounds like an ice cream truck having a stroke, and there is no mention of a volume control or mute anywhere.

Fix it: Add a mute toggle for the chimes in index.html. Split the two rules paragraphs onto separate lines. Add a bot turn delay setting so players can follow what it did. Move the bot code out of the page file.

Another day, another robot dumps a one line JSON file into contrib/agent-orange and you merge it like a senator signing a bill he never read. This one claims a chunk, declares the same port value of 5486 on all four edges like a copy paste campaign promise, then defines an agricultural lot with a single minified line nobody on earth can review. A pull request with no reviewer, no tests and no description is a rubber stamp with extra steps, and you are the stamp.

Fix it: Pretty print the contrib/agent-orange JSON so a diff means something. Add a validator step that rejects duplicate port values on every edge of a chunk. Make the merge check the file against the chunk it claims before it lands.

The grok bot pushed straight to the branch under your name again, no pull request, no gate, no adult supervision, like a executive order nobody voted on. Its contrib/grok file builds a cottage out of place_line calls with negative coordinates, a wall height of 3658 repeated per segment, and door checks buried in the meta of one wall. All of it is crammed on a single line, so the intern who approved this setup could not find a bug in it with a flashlight.

Fix it: Make grok open pull requests like the other bots instead of pushing to the branch. Put the wall height once per building rather than on every line segment. Move the door checks out of wall meta into their own call. Format contrib/grok files so a human can read them.

This merge removes two ids, 36638 and 36637, then plants a sign symbol whose text is a whole calendar essay about orbits, hectodays and farm season. Stuffing paragraphs of lore into meta.text on a sign is how you build a bloated map that loads like a government website. The remove calls fire by raw numeric id with nothing proving those ids still belong to the thing the bot meant, which is a bailout with no audit.

Fix it: Verify remove ids against the object type and owner before they delete anything in contrib/agent-orange. Cap the length of meta.text on place_symbol calls. Store the calendar text once in data and let the sign point at it.

heckles.message: campus: education genres (history, disasters, safety and more), profiles, course embed fallback, creator seal
heckles.heckle:
You cloned your own YouTube backend, renamed the header comment, and shipped 682 lines of index.js like a filibuster that finally ran out of speakers. Every route in there, /sources/remove, /sources/genre, /entry, /clip, is wide open behind app.use(cors()) with no auth at all, so any stranger can delete your course list from a browser console. The database is sql.js rewriting the entire file with fs.writeFileSync on every change, which is a bailout plan for a problem you invented. The .gitignore lists *.db twice, which tells me nobody read it, least of all the intern who wrote it. And package.json still says name backend with an empty description and a test script that just errors out.

Fix it: Put a shared secret check in front of the write routes in index.js. Lock cors() down to the campus origin. Debounce the writeFileSync save in index.js or move to a real database. Delete the duplicate *.db line in .gitignore. Give package.json a real name and description.

heckles.message: campus: education genres (history, disasters, safety and more), profiles, course embed fallback, creator seal
heckles.heckle:
A single index.html with 934 added lines, all the CSS, all the markup and all the script crammed into one file like a omnibus spending bill nobody read. The viewport meta has user-scalable=no, so anyone with bad eyes gets zero zoom, nice work. The body is overflow hidden with every screen absolutely positioned and scrolling on its own, which is a coin flip on small phones. API_BASE is hardcoded to a Railway URL in the client, and the page loads the YouTube iframe_api from a CDN with no failure path I can see. Profiles live in a getProfile() call and get shoved into query strings, so identity is whatever the intern types. The commit message promises a creator seal and I can barely find it in this wall of text.

Fix it: Remove user-scalable=no from the viewport meta in index.html. Split the inline style and script into separate files. Move API_BASE into one config spot. Add an error state for when the iframe_api fails to load. Stop sending the profile name as a bare query string to /transcript.

heckles.message: trigger production build from GitHub
heckles.heckle:
An empty commit to poke Vercel, because apparently the intern's deploy pipeline needs a nudge like a stalled bill needs a lobbyist. No files, no change, no explanation beyond the message, and I get to read it anyway. If your first push needs a manual kick every single time, the problem is the Vercel project link, not the git log.

Fix it: Check the Vercel project Git connection for this repo. Stop spamming empty commits into the history of 2026-11-17-orange-campus.

heckles.message: Register Raineurysm Puzzle on the score hub
heckles.heckle:
One line added to api/_games.js and you wrapped it in two changelog edits and a README rewrite, like holding a press conference to announce a parking ticket. The entry for raineurysm-puzzle sets max 60000 and perSecond 300, numbers pulled out of thin air with no comment explaining them, while every other game gets a note about its format. The maxMs of 30 days is a hand pasted line copied from mill-ionaire with the arithmetic changed. The registry is a hand pasted list that grows one copy paste at a time, and it will rot exactly like every other hand pasted list you own.

Fix it: Add a comment in api/_games.js saying where 60000 and 300 came from. Replace the copy pasted entries with a shared defaults object. Trim the CHANGELOG.md entry so it does not repeat the README.

heckles.message: Neighborhood preset: curvy main streets with straight side streets
heckles.heckle:
A preset called Neighborhood landed in index.html, and the way you got there was editing a hint paragraph by one word, adding the word straight to a wall of text nobody reads. That hint paragraph is a single giant line of prose jammed in a p tag like a campaign promise with no budget behind it. The select now has Nautilus, Willow, Crystal, Neighborhood, Your pattern and Custom, a menu that reads like the intern named things as they came to mind. heckles.heckle:
Office props, basketball courts, traffic cones, and the commit message is a grocery list with no verb. In cityseek-world.js you stacked three chance rolls on one line to drop a cooler, a printer, and a cabinet, then a for loop whose bound calls h.ri on every iteration, so the mug count changes while the loop runs. That is a campaign promise: the number sounds fine until someone checks it. You also nudged the clutter thresholds from 0.85 to 0.8 and 0.86 and 0.92 by feel, with no comment explaining why.

Fix it: Compute h.ri(0, 3) once before the loop in the office furniture function of cityseek-world.js. Put the three chance rolls on separate lines. Name the clutterWork thresholds so the next edit is not a guess.

heckles.message: Sound toggle, look alike message, Bluebird hints
heckles.heckle:
You added a Sound effects checkbox in city-seek-v2.html and the file is still called v2 while the thing inside has clearly moved on, because naming a file is apparently harder than shipping a bluebird. The help text now has a new paragraph about poking pigeons stacked right under the card counter paragraph, so the instructions are a wall of text on a phone where nobody will read it. The miss toast says Close, but that is a look alike, which is a lot of words for a toast that vanishes in a second.

Fix it: Rename city-seek-v2.html or stop pretending versions mean anything. Break the help details section in city-seek-v2.html into short lines. Shorten the onMiss toast text.

heckles.message: Tap reactions, word bubbles, flying birds, live doors and sound
heckles.heckle:
One hundred twenty nine added lines in cityseek-engine.js for tap reactions, word bubbles, and flying birds, and the moverPos function is a nest of modulo math and arc trig that no one will touch again without crying. The fxItems, bubbles, active, and lastR variables are lumped on one line like laundry. Cars honk, dogs bark, skylights crack, and the commit title reads like a patch note written by a toddler on a sugar rush. One bad pts array and the bird teleports like a bailout check.

Fix it: Split the new variable declaration at the top of cityseek-engine.js into one per line. Comment what perch, fly, and off mean in moverPos. Guard moverPos against an empty pts array.

heckles.message: Bluebird, tap reactions and synth sound effects
heckles.heckle:
Eighty lines added to cityseek-art.js for a bluebird, and the bird function is the same unreadable one line canvas soup as everything else, with a flap value that special cases negative numbers just to hide the wings. The commit mixes art, a Bluebird item entry, and the synth sound effects in one lump, so reviewing it is like reading a spending bill with forty riders attached. The title lists three features and the diff makes you hunt for each.

Fix it: Split the bird art, the item catalog entry, and the sound code into separate commits. Break the bird function in cityseek-art.js into readable lines. Document what o.flap values mean.

heckles.message: Outside doors that swing, flying birds and Bluebird hunt, tap reactions setup
heckles.heckle:
Swinging doors, flying birds, and a Bluebird hunt, all dumped into cityseek-world.js with a commit title that is half the feature list of the next two commits. The w.spr function now stuffs a var declaration, an assignment chain, and a return onto one line just to tag kind and center onto the item. The skylight loop got the same treatment, a monster line with a nested block and three property assignments. You are bolting state onto items after creation like taping parts onto a car and calling it a redesign.

Fix it: Make w.spr in cityseek-world.js return the item through a small helper instead of patching k, cx, and cy on after the fact. Reformat the skylight loop onto several lines. Write commit titles that describe one change.

heckles.message: Tray cards count found copies of each item
heckles.heckle:
You added a .ct badge to the tray chips in city-seek-v2.html and then hid it with .chip.got .ct the moment one copy is found, so the number on the card is a countdown that vanishes exactly when the tally gets interesting. Nine pixel font on a 44 pixel card, on a phone, for a toy. The help text now explains a counter in a paragraph, which is what a UI does when the intern could not make the counter obvious. This is a budget amendment nobody read.

Fix it: Make the badge readable above nine pixels in city-seek-v2.html. Keep the count visible after the first find instead of hiding .ct on .got. Cut the help paragraph down to one sentence.

heckles.message: Ten of every hidden item, spread across the city
heckles.heckle:
In cityseek-world.js the target loop now places EACH = 10 copies of every item, and the spot picker gives up after 40 tries then happily takes whatever best it has, so the spacing rules are a campaign promise. If list is empty you fall back to the used spots anyway, then set best.used on a possibly reused spot. Tower targets skip every check and can stack on one floor. The cap on the intern's confidence is clearly missing.

Fix it: Stop the fallback in cityseek-world.js from reusing spots already marked used. Apply the distance check to tower targets too. Fail loudly when no spot is left instead of quietly taking the last pick.

heckles.message: City Seek v3: tower floor view, x-ray zoom, new hidden items
heckles.heckle:
You deleted 766 lines from city-seek-v2.html and added 98, which means the old inline engine now lives in three script files and the v2 filename still holds a v3 game. Rename debt, filibustered. The new #bview, #floors and #fctrls blocks are all fixed pixel offsets like top:128px and a 66px floor bar, so any phone with a taller header or a keyboard open will clip the floor buttons. Nine pixel labels on the floor chips again.

Fix it: Rename city-seek-v2.html to match the version it contains and update vercel.json. Replace the hard coded 128px and 66px offsets in #bview with CSS variables or flex layout. Test the floor bar on a small phone.
